chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him)
That he (peace be upon him) did not prostrate on the sleeves (of the garment) nor on the turban.
ai.seo_question: What should be avoided when placing the forehead during prostration in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) clarifies the technical details of prostration by specifying that the forehead must rest directly on the natural surface of the turbah or ground, rather than on the fabric of the sleeves (kumman) or the turban (imamah) itself. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the necessity of the forehead touching the actual place of prostration (mujib) with minimal obstruction, distinguishing it from the permissibility of prostrating on other body parts or clothing in different schools of thought. It highlights the precision with which the Ahl al-Bayt preserved the Sunnah regarding the physical mechanics of prayer.
